_comment: End-to-end prediction transcripts replayed by _shared/lua/test/llm_engine_transcript.lua against the real macOS and Linux engines on recording fakes of the three ports. A scenario gives a config (the menu's debounce in ms, prediction count and prompt, an optional user prompt, and watch_timers_ms: the only timer delays recorded, so the engines' own watchdogs and spinners stay out), steps (keystroke: the whole typed buffer after one keystroke; elapse_ms: time passing, which runs the timers that fall due; answer: the provider answers request N; toggle_live: the live binding with its parameter; delete_prompt: the user deletes a prompt), and expect: the port calls in order. Calls: timer.after with delay_ms; http.post with max_tokens (the symbols base, batch:N and rewrite are resolved from the shared token budget); tooltip.show with the number of candidates and the info pieces ($model is the model the shared Cerebras entry defaults to; $profile:ID is the prompt's name as the driver's menu spells it, short-label rule applied). Only a render that is not a loading placeholder is recorded.

drivers.windows: Not ported yet: the AutoHotkey engine would have to expose the same three ports (a timer, an HTTP client and a tooltip renderer it can be given fakes of) and replay every scenario; today its timers and requests are called directly.

differences.seams: Linux hands the engine its scheduler and its overlay through init and its HTTP client through the module the remote backend requires; macOS has no init injection for them, so its world replaces adapters.timer_scheduler.after, the remote backend's inference client and ui.tooltip in place. The ports are the same three; only the way a fake is put in differs.
differences.repaint: macOS paints the final answer a second time after its success callback commits; the screen does not change, so the macOS world records one tooltip call for two identical consecutive paints. Linux paints once.
differences.batch_reveal: macOS reveals a batch prediction by prediction on zero-delay timers; its world runs the timers an answer arms. Linux shows the batch at once.
differences.info_bar_join: The pieces are compared, not the joined text: macOS joins with an em dash and Linux with a middle dot and adds i/n (see request_plan_info_bar_vectors.json).
